learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialization, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advancements.
Be aware of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; select and apply established analytical, computational, and experimental methods appropriately, and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics of their specialization.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes specific to their specialization.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within the engineering field and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to keep up to date with new developments in science and technology.
Know the biosignals generated by the body and understand their main characteristics.
Design data processing algorithms that allow extracting the desired characteristics from a particular biosignal.

teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Presentation in the classroom in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Individual study and work, tests, exams, and/or control points
Performance of exercises individually and in teams

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for evaluating technical competencies
Project/PBL work (technical capacity, involvement, results, documentation, presentation, and technical defense)
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: For the evaluation of technical competencies related to RAB03, there are individual written and oral tests (70%) and project work (30%). For the evaluation of technical competencies related to RAB04, there are individual written and oral tests (40%), reports on various practices (30%), and project work (30%). Recovery mechanisms for written and oral technical competency tests are available. The syllabus does not specify how the assessments for RAB03 and RAB04 combine for the final course grade, nor does it detail minimum marks or an overall grading formula.
